# Kyoto Budget Trip Plan: 5 Days for 2 Adults

A relaxed, temple-and-garden-focused Kyoto plan for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-14** with a **USD 1,800 total budget** excluding international flights. I’ve kept each day under roughly **12,000 steps** by grouping sights by area and using transit between clusters.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Cost Plan

| Day | Area Focus | Main Plan | Transit Suggestion | Est. Cost for 2 | Rainy-Day Backup |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Day 1: Apr 10 | Higashiyama | Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, Yasaka Shrine, Maruyama Park | Kyoto City Bus + short taxi if needed | **USD 180** | Kyoto National Museum + covered lanes around Gion |
| Day 2: Apr 11 | Arashiyama | Bamboo Grove, Tenryu-ji, Okochi Sanso Garden, riverside walk | JR Sagano Line + local bus | **USD 220** | Arashiyama Monkey Park skip; do train museum or cafe time near Kyoto Station |
| Day 3: Apr 12 | Central Kyoto | Nishiki Market, Teramachi/Shinkyogoku shopping, Nijo Castle area | Subway + walking | **USD 210** | Indoor shopping arcades, Kyoto International Manga Museum |
| Day 4: Apr 13 | Northern Kyoto | Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji, Daitoku-ji area gardens/temples | Bus + taxi between temple clusters | **USD 190** | Daitoku-ji subtemples, tea house stops, department store browsing |
| Day 5: Apr 14 | Southern/West Kyoto | Fushimi Inari early morning, then relaxed farewell lunch and souvenir stop | JR Nara Line + subway | **USD 170** | Kyoto Railway Museum or Kyoto Tower area |

## Detailed Daily Plan

### Day 1: Higashiyama Temples and Old Streets
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Start at **Kiyomizu-dera** early to avoid crowds; then walk down through **Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka**.
- Afternoon: Visit **Yasaka Shrine** and stroll **Maruyama Park** at a slow pace.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Visit **Yasaka Shrine** and stroll **Maruyama Park** at a slow pace, Kyoto, Japan
- Dinner: Try **yudofu** or a **kaiseki-style set lunch/dinner** in Gion or Higashiyama.
- Transit: Use city bus to Kiyomizu area, then mostly walk downhill; taxi back if legs feel tired.
- Estimated cost: Entry, local transit, snacks, and meals for 2: **USD 180**
- Rainy-day backup: **Kyoto National Museum** plus indoor tea break in Gion.
- Step target: **8,000–10,000**

### Day 2: Arashiyama Gardens and Riverside
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Go early to the **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** and **Tenryu-ji**.
- Afternoon: Spend time at **Okochi Sanso Garden** for a quieter, scenic break; finish with the **Togetsukyo Bridge** riverside area.
- Dinner: Casual **soba**, **tofu dishes**, or **yuba** near Arashiyama or back in central Kyoto.
- Transit: JR Sagano Line to Saga-Arashiyama, then walk and use short bus/taxi hops if needed.
- Estimated cost: Temple/garden entries, train, meals, coffee, and snacks for 2: **USD 220**
- Rainy-day backup: Skip the long outdoor walk and do a **train museum or cafe-hopping afternoon** near Kyoto Station.
- Step target: **9,000–11,000**

### Day 3: Market Food and Relaxed Shopping Afternoon
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- Morning: Start at **Nishiki Market** for local bites and browsing.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning: Start at **Nishiki Market** for local bites and browsing, Kyoto, Japan
- Afternoon: Make this your **shopping day** in **Teramachi** and **Shinkyogoku** arcades; keep it easy and indoor-friendly.
- Dinner: Choose a **ramen** or **izakaya-style** meal with small plates.
- Transit: Subway to Karasuma/Oike, then walk through the covered shopping streets.
- Estimated cost: Food, shopping buffer, transit, and dinner for 2: **USD 210**
- Rainy-day backup: Stay entirely in the arcades and add the **Kyoto International Manga Museum**.
- Step target: **7,000–9,500**

### Day 4: Northern Kyoto Temples and Quiet Gardens
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** early, then continue to **Ryoan-ji**.
- Afternoon: Slow down in the **Daitoku-ji** area, choosing one or two subtemples or garden stops rather than rushing.
- Dinner: Go for a simple **donburi**, **tempura set**, or a neighborhood **udon** dinner.
- Transit: Use buses, but consider one taxi segment between temple clusters to save steps and time.
- Estimated cost: Admissions, transit, meals, and a taxi segment for 2: **USD 190**
- Rainy-day backup: Focus on **indoor temple halls**, tea rooms, and a department-store food floor.
- Step target: **8,000–10,500**

### Day 5: Fushimi Inari and Farewell Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Morning: Arrive early at **Fushimi Inari Taisha** and do a shorter torii-gate walk, not the full summit, to keep steps low.
- Afternoon: Return to central Kyoto for a relaxed last lunch and souvenir stop near Kyoto Station.
- Dinner: Final meal can be **kaisendon**, **tofu**, or a polished **set meal** depending on your departure timing.
- Transit: JR Nara Line to Inari Station; subway or taxi back after the shrine visit.
- Estimated cost: Transit, meals, souvenirs, and small extras for 2: **USD 170**
- Rainy-day backup: **Kyoto Railway Museum** or **Kyoto Tower** area instead of the shrine walk.
- Step target: **6,000–9,000**

## Budget Check for 2 Adults

- Lodging: **USD 650–850** total for 4 nights in a clean mid-range hotel or well-rated business hotel
- Local transit: **USD 80–140**
- Admissions and gardens/temples: **USD 60–120**
- Meals and snacks: **USD 450–650**
- Shopping/souvenirs buffer: **USD 100–200**
- Contingency: **USD 100–150**

**Estimated total:** **USD 1,440–2,110**

To stay within your **USD 1,800** cap, aim for:
- Lodging around **USD 700–780**
- Meals around **USD 500–560**
- Keep shopping to **USD 100–150**
- Use a mix of buses, subway, and a couple of short taxis

## Best Fit for Your Priorities

- **Temples/gardens:** Days 1, 2, and 4 are the strongest
- **Local food:** Days 1, 2, and 3 have the best food opportunities
- **Relaxed shopping:** Day 3 is your dedicated low-stress afternoon
- **Low walking:** The route is clustered by neighborhood, with transit between areas and a shorter Fushimi Inari visit
